Diarrhoea Diarrhoea is characterised by liquid stools and increased stool weight and frequency of defaecation. Although diar- rhoea is commonly associated with infection (see Gastro- enteritis, p.171), it may also result from the accumulation of nonabsorbed osmotically active solutes in the gastroin- testinal lumen, as in lactase deficiency, or from the gas- trointestinal effects of secretory stimuli other than the en- terotoxins from an infection. It may also occur when intestinal motility or morphology is altered.
